def: The 64-byte command structure the host writes into a Submission Queue slot; the controller fetches it and executes the command it describes.
The 16-byte structure the controller writes into a Completion Queue to report a command's status; it carries the SQ head pointer, SQ identifier, command identifier, phase tag and status.
A bit in Read and Write commands (CDW12 bit 30). For a Write, the controller must commit that command's data and metadata to non-volatile media before completing it.

A controller cache whose contents may be lost on power failure. Identify Controller's VWC field reports its presence (bit 0) and, since NVMe 1.4, whether Flush with NSID FFFFFFFFh is supported (bits 2:1). Feature 06h enables or disables it.

The NVMe I/O command (opcode 00h) that commits to non-volatile media the data and metadata of writes to a namespace that completed before the Flush was submitted. It carries no data and is not a barrier for later commands.
NVM Command Set command (opcode 09h) carrying up to 256 sixteen-byte LBA ranges with attributes; with the Deallocate attribute it tells the controller the ranges are no longer needed.

Removing the mapping between logical blocks and stored data so the controller no longer has to preserve it; requested with Dataset Management (AD attribute) or Write Zeroes with the deallocate option. Reads then return what DLFEAT reports.
Identify Namespace field whose bits 2:0 report what reads of deallocated logical blocks return: 000b not reported, 001b all 00h bytes, 010b all FFh bytes.
The ATA name for telling an SSD which logical blocks hold no useful data; used loosely for the same idea in any protocol (NVMe Dataset Management Deallocate, SCSI UNMAP, Linux discard).
The Linux block-layer operation that tells a device a range of sectors is unused; the NVMe driver turns it into Dataset Management with the Deallocate attribute.
SSD firmware that maps logical block addresses to physical NAND locations, writes out of place, and runs garbage collection and wear leveling.
The SSD's process of reclaiming erase blocks by copying still-valid pages elsewhere and erasing the block; its cost grows with the fraction of valid pages in the blocks it reclaims.

Bytes programmed to NAND divided by bytes the host wrote; extra writes come from garbage-collection relocation and metadata. For greedy GC, roughly 1/(1-u) where u is the valid fraction of reclaimed blocks.
Physical flash capacity beyond the user-visible capacity, used by the FTL as working space; deallocated space acts as additional, dynamic over-provisioning.
Energy storage (typically capacitors) that keeps an SSD running long enough after external power loss to commit buffered data; drives with full PLP often report no volatile write cache.
Identify Controller field whose bits report support for optional commands such as Compare, Write Uncorrectable, Dataset Management (bit 2) and Write Zeroes.
The 0's based transfer length in Read and Write commands (CDW12 bits 15:0): NLB = 7 means 8 logical blocks.
The first logical block a Read or Write accesses, held in CDW10 (low) and CDW11 (high).
PCIe Device Control setting that caps the size of each Memory Read request a function issues; it shapes how many requests a device needs to fetch NVMe write data.
The address alignment (64 or 128 bytes) at which a completer may split the completions answering one Memory Read request.
Identify Controller field (0's based, in logical blocks) giving the write size guaranteed to be written atomically even across a power failure; namespaces may report NAWUPF.

exp: Deallocated or Unwritten Logical Block Error
def: An Error Recovery feature option that makes reads of deallocated or never-written logical blocks complete with an error status instead of returning data.
Identify Namespace field (NVMe 1.4 and later) giving the deallocation size the controller prefers; paired with NPDA, the preferred alignment.
SMART / Health Information log counter of power losses that occurred without a completed shutdown notification (CC.SHN / CSTS.SHST).
NVM Command Set command (opcode 08h) that sets a range of logical blocks to read as zeros without transferring data; it may deallocate when the host allows and the controller supports it.
The earliest observation that deviates from expected behavior in a failure; often earlier than, and different from, the first logged error.
A known-good capture of an operation used as the reference when comparing a failing capture.
